guarantees.claim: idle is the logical AND of !reg_fifo_wvalid, !fifo_rvalid, hmac_core_idle, and sha_core_idle.
idle_d is assigned as the mubi4-bool-to-mubi encoding of idle.

assumptions.claim: reg_fifo_wvalid, fifo_rvalid, hmac_core_idle, and sha_core_idle accurately reflect the internal FIFO and core idle conditions.
assumptions.cond: whenever idle is used to derive multi-bit integrity state
assumptions.risk: an incorrect idle value propagates a false idle condition, potentially causing downstream safety logic to enter an unsafe state

assumptions.claim: Inputs must be stable around the capturing clock edge to avoid glitches on idle_d.
assumptions.cond: when idle_d is sampled synchronously by downstream logic
assumptions.risk: a glitch on idle_d may produce a transient non-mubi4-valid pattern that could be misinterpreted as a fatal integrity error or cause a spurious alert

uncertain_points.claim: Integrity of hmac_core_idle and sha_core_idle is not verified locally; a stuck-at fault in those signals could cause idle_d to permanently encode a false idle.
uncertain_points.cond: if the source modules of these signals do not provide similar multi-bit integrity protection
uncertain_points.risk: the system may continuously believe the HMAC or SHA core is idle, compromising secure processing

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational path from inputs to idle_d may cause glitches if any input changes asynchronously; idle_d may momentarily take an illegal mubi encoding.
uncertain_points.cond: if inputs are not synchronized and change near the sampling edge
uncertain_points.risk: a transient illegal encoding could be detected as a fatal alert or trigger unexpected state transitions in a multi-bit safety monitor
